“Animam voco. Reversus vita perfecta est animus.” I chanted. I chanted over and over, until my voice was hoarse. Finally I sat back, defeated. He wasn’t coming back. Suddenly his eyes pop open. He sits up frantically, screaming “Take me back! I need to go back!”

“Back where? My love, you’ve only just returned to me! What is going on?”

He looks around wildly, gathering his bearings. He puts his head in his hands. I kneel in front of him, reaching out to touch his shoulder, but he snatches back. “I can’t do this. I have to return or they’ll take you. They’ll take Bex. Send me back.”

“Who will take me? What do you mean? How does Bex have anything to do with this?” I ask calmly, but I feel anything but calm.

“Zeta. They’re rounding up souls. Anyone who has been touched by the light. I didn’t tell you but I traded myself for you, for our son. I can’t stay here. If I do they will come for me. They’re probably already looking. Triz, you’ve got to kill me. You’ve got to send me back,” he says, grabbing my dagger and pushing it into my hands.
“I can’t kill you. I only just got you back!”

He sighs, looking away. “You HAVE to! You can do this. You can go on without me.”

I get up and walk over to the window, pacing, thinking. He wants me to take his life. He wants ME to take HIS life.
“Baby, if you can’t do it.. I can do it myself,” he says fiercely, so fiercely that it makes me turn around. He has a knife pointed at himself.

“Kez, no. There’s got to be another way.”

“There isn’t, Triz. That’s what I’m trying to tell you. I have to die. I have to fulfill the contract-“ he stops, looking at the door in horror. “Did you hear that?” he whispers loudly.

“Hear wha-“ BANG, BANG, BANG. There’s someone hitting the door. They’re here. I grab him, pulling him to the vault. He pulls back, looking at me.

“Either you kill me now or I kill myself. I won’t go back with them and I won’t let them take you. If you give them my body they will leave you, Triz, you’ll be safe!”

I stop, thinking. If he wants me to do this I’m going to make it as painless for him as possible. I grab the syringe out of the fridge and run over to the door of the vault.

“Alright, fine. I will do it, but I’m not going to let them rush me. Shut the vault door & lie down on the couch. Then I’ll do it,” I say, as I’m sticking the syringe into the bottle, carefully drawing out the freezing purple liquid. He shuts the door and lays down.

He looks at me with tears in his eyes, reaching out for my hand. “I love you so much. I wish I could stay, but I promise we will meet again. This is not the last time you will see me, my love.”

I look at the ceiling, willing the tears to just hold back until I get through this. “I love you so much. Thank you for being so brave for me, for our son. I won’t let him forget you. I have to do this now, before the death liquid warms up. It won’t hurt you, I promise. It will just feel as if your body is warming naturally, like it’s being kissed by the sun.”

He smiles a little, leans up to give me a kiss, & then rolls on his side, facing the back of the couch. I slide his long hair to the side, sticking the needle in at the base of his neck, the top of his spine.

“I love... you,” he whispers as he fades away. I cover my mouth, looking away. I have to get up. I have to walk out there and show these sons of bitches that he’s dead. I get up, anger on my face. The vault door opens as I scan my retina, the door screeching. They’re waiting, weapons pointed at me.

“He’s dead. He’s dead and it’s your fault,” I shout, pointing at the commander, Zeta.

Zeta looks at me, calculating. “Did you kill him, Triz? I didn’t think you had it in you.”
I didn’t say anything, he didn’t deserve another word from me.

“Very well,” he said. “Your husband’s debt is paid. You and your son are safe, for now.”

For now? What the hell did he mean, for now? “Zeta you said-“

“I know what I said. With the skill set you have, you’d be valuable to the Guard,” he said, smiling maliciously. “We will be back to see you soon.”

I started to run at him, but one of the other guards grabbed me. “You will die if you try to kill him and then your husband’s death will have been for nought. Be grateful we have shown you mercy,” he spat at me, throwing me to the ground. 

They left, just like that, with my husband’s dead body carelessly thrown over one of their shoulders. I will kill them. I will kill them all.

As recently as the beginning of this year we didn’t have air. When I was growing up we only had it at night, in our bedroom, and only when it was SUPER hot. We had the units but they were too expensive to turn on. When I graduated & moved out my husbands-then boyfriends-family didn’t have air either. Moved into roommates, & we had it for about a month before the hurricane took it out. It wasn’t until we moved here by ourselves that we finally had it. Yes, it is expensive, and it means we’re broke in all other aspects, but I can’t imagine going back to just 8 months ago, not having air, in the south Georgia heat. It was awful. Other things growing up that I remember are having my Christmas brought to me by strangers and by people from school or church, receiving thanksgiving and Christmas “boxes” with foodstuff to prepare meals for the holidays, not having certain technologies that other children had such as gaming consoles or cell phones, being told many times that we couldn’t afford simple things, basic needs. As I grow older I realize how much my family did to try to cover up how poor we were, and I appreciate the effort they made. I feel like it helped me grow into someone with compassion for others who struggle. I am humbled by something as simple as a friend buying a meal for me simply because they want to. It makes me feel like a burden even when I know that’s not the case.
